subject: Stepwise adoption MAP & monthly throughput plan
messages:
From: Julia Carr <julia@nimhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP & evaluation — suggested acceptance gates and monthly TPMP targets

Hi Mina / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our exec team liked the latency and the prefix-caching story — we
want to move from evaluation to a staged production rollout, but need to lock down the MAP (mutual
action plan) and the financials tied to milestones. High-level asks from our side: 

- A 3-month evaluation window (non-production) with a low entry commit for tokens so we can stress test
  integrations.
- A beta ramp month where we move to 50% of the target TPM, then two production months at 100% and
  150% capacity respectively.
- Discount ladder tied to steady-state monthly tokens (thresholds at 1M, 3M, 6M tokens).
- A credit/rollback mechanism if acceptance gates fail (POC acceptance criteria attached).

Can you send a skeleton MAP that maps milestones (evaluation, beta, prod) to concrete monthly token
commitments and baseline pricing? Procurement also asked for an indicative schedule so they can align
approval and PO timing. I attached last quarter's trial usage to give a baseline.

Thanks — Julia

Attachments: trial_usage.csv (8KB)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Julia Carr <julia@nimhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & evaluation — suggested acceptance gates and monthly TPMP targets

Julia — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing trial usage. 

High level reply first, then I attached a draft MAP that we can iterate on: 

- Proposal: 1 month evaluation (no committed production tokens), 1 month beta (soft commit at 50% of target),
  then a 3-month staged production ramp (Month 1 = 75% of target, Month 2 = 100%, Month 3 = 125%)
  to account for warm-up and cache effects.
- Pricing: we'll offer a stepped discount schedule. Example (indicative): list price $0.12/1k tokens;
  1M+ => 8% off, 3M+ => 15% off, 6M+ => 22% off.
- If an acceptance gate fails (performance or integration), we propose a remediation window and a one-time
  service credit equal to 10% of that month’s committed spend (as an alternative to a full refund).
- Procurement timeline: if we sign an SOW by 2026-06-10 we can target a go-live for 2026-06-30 with kick-off
  week of 2026-06-15.

I attached: draft_map_v1.pdf and SOW_Nimbus_v1.docx. Ben — flagged for pricing confirmation and Aditya for
contract language.

Thanks,
Mina

Attachments: draft_map_v1.pdf (74KB), SOW_Nimbus_v1.docx (32KB)
From: Mark Lewis <mark.lewis@nimhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Carr <julia@nimhealth.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & evaluation — suggested acceptance gates and monthly TPMP targets

Mina/Ben — quick technical note from our side. The proposed ramp looks fine but two asks: 

1) Burst buffer: in month-to-month reality, our traffic is spiky. We need a short-term burst allowance (
   e.g., +30% for up to 48 hours) that doesn’t immediately push us into a higher committed tier or a
   surprise overage charge.
2) Acceptance gate slippage: if we miss an acceptance gate due to a Redwood-side regression (e.g.,
   quality or latency regression tied to a new model kernel), we need an option to pause the ramp +
   additional credits to offset our operational uplift while we re-run validations.

Procurement also wants to shorten the internal approval window — they asked if you can provide an
illustrative PO template and a single-point contact for SLA exceptions.

—Mark
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Mark Lewis <mark.lewis@nimhealth.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 26 May 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & evaluation — suggested acceptance gates and monthly TPMP targets

Mark — thanks for the feedback. A few clarifications and concrete commitments from our side below.

- Burst buffer: we can include a built-in 30% daily burst allowance for the first 3 months of production.
  Usage beyond that window will follow normal overage rates, but we won’t auto-escalate you into a higher
  committed tier mid-month — overages will be billed separately at list minus any applicable tier discount.

- Credits for regressions: we agree to a remediation path. If a regression is traced to our runtime or model
  change and your acceptance gate fails as a result, Redwood will provide a remediation credit equal to 15%
  of that month’s committed spend (higher than the standard 10% we mentioned) and prioritize a rollback or
  patch. We’ll add a short SLA exception clause in the SOW for this scenario.

- Pricing (finalized example for the MAP):
  * Evaluation month: no committed spend, usage at list ($0.14/1k tokens)
  * Beta (soft commit at 50% of target): $0.12/1k tokens base pricing
  * Production tiers (committed monthly):
    - 1M–2.99M tokens: $0.11/1k (8% discount)
    - 3M–5.99M tokens: $0.095/1k (20% discount)
    - 6M+ tokens: $0.0875/1k (26% discount)

  We can also offer a one-time onboarding credit of $7,500 applied to the first invoice if the SOW is signed
  by 2026-06-10.

Attached a more detailed pricing matrix. Ben — can you confirm these prices are budget-approved?

—Aditya

Attachments: pricing_sheet_v3.csv (12KB)
From: Julia Carr <julia@nimhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Lewis <mark.lewis@nimhealth.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2026 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & evaluation — suggested acceptance gates and monthly TPMP targets

Thanks — this is very helpful and straightforward. We’ve reviewed the draft MAP and the pricing sheet;
procurement is comfortable moving forward with the proposed staged ramp and the higher remediation credit
(15%) for vendor regressions. A few final notes: 

- We accept the 30% burst buffer for the first 3 months.
- Please include the onboarding credit in the first invoice.
- PO attached (PO_43921.pdf). Procurement will issue the PO once we have a final SOW with the SLA
  exception clause and an estimated invoice schedule.

If you can circulate an updated SOW with the SA/exception language by Friday (2026-05-30) we’ll route
for signature and target the kick-off week of 2026-06-15 as suggested.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
—Julia

Attachments: PO_43921.pdf (22KB)
